record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: For a general infinite-dimensional control system, does every input-to-state stability Lyapunov function given in implication form also admit an equivalent dissipative-form characterization, without imposing the restrictive extra assumptions currently needed? Equivalently, is implication-form ISS Lyapunov theory fully equivalent to dissipative-form ISS Lyapunov theory in infinite dimensions, as it is for ordinary differential equations under reasonable regularity assumptions?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.17. For infinite-dimensional systems, it is easy to see that if V is an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form, then it is an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form. It is, however, an open question, whether the converse implication holds unless quite restrictive requirements on Σ and Lyapunov function V are imposed, see [167, Theorem 3.4].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space (the state space) and $U$ a normed space of input values, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$. Consider a control system $\Sigma$ with state trajectories $x(\cdot;x_0,u)\in X$ defined for initial state $x_0\in X$ and input $u\in\mathcal{U}$. Recall the comparison-function classes $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, and $\mathcal{KL}$.

A continuous functional $V:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ that is locally Lipschitz on $X\setminus\{0\}$ and satisfies
$$\psi_1(\|x\|_X)\leq V(x)\leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X),\qquad \forall x\in X,$$
for some $\psi_1,\psi_2\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$, is called:

(a) an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form for $\Sigma$ if there exist $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal{K}$ such that for almost every $t\geq 0$, along every trajectory,
$$\dot V(x(t))\leq -\alpha(\|x(t)\|_X)+\sigma(\|u(t)\|_U);$$

(b) an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form for $\Sigma$ if there exist $\chi\in\mathcal{K}$ and $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$\|x\|_X\geq \chi(\|u(t)\|_U)\;\Longrightarrow\;\dot V(x(t))\leq -\alpha(\|x(t)\|_X).$$

It is straightforward that (a) implies (b). For finite-dimensional ODE systems with sufficient regularity, the converse also holds (the two notions are equivalent).

Question: Is it true, for every infinite-dimensional control system $\Sigma$ on a Banach space $X$ (in a suitable general class encompassing well-posed evolution equations), that the existence of an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form implies the existence of an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form, without imposing restrictive additional regularity or structural assumptions on $\Sigma$ or $V$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., a 2025 paper in Mathematics of Control, Signals, and Systems on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems, and 2021–2025 works on infinite networks) continues to construct dissipative-form Lyapunov functions only under additional assumptions, treating the general equivalence in infinite dimensions as still unresolved. While equivalence has been settled for (continuous) discrete-time systems and via "strong implication form" notions, no general equivalence theorem for infinite-dimensional continuous-time systems without restrictive hypotheses appears in the located sources, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems under specific structural assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still requires structural assumptions, suggesting general equivalence remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: ISS small-gain criteria for infinite networks with linear gains
status_evidence.snippet: Provides implication-form ISS Lyapunov function and constructs dissipative form under mild extra assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Passage from implication to dissipative form is done only under additional assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Equivalent types of ISS Lyapunov functions for discontinuous discrete-time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses equivalence between implication-form and dissipation-form ISS-Lyapunov functions, primarily in discrete-time settings.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalence is established for some discrete-time settings but not generally for infinite-dimensional continuous-time systems.
